concepts.name: ADB's Founding and Historical Context
key_dimensions: Established in 1966 — distinguishing from World Bank (1944) and AIIB (2016)
Role of ECAFE (UN Economic Commission for Asia and the Far East) as precursor body
Cold War geopolitical context and US/Japan's strategic role in founding
Headquarters in Manila, Philippines — contrast with other MDB headquarters

concepts.name: ADB Membership Structure and Voting Power
key_dimensions: 67 members: 48 regional + 19 non-regional — UPSC trap on 'Asian-only' misconception
Japan and USA as the two largest shareholders (~15.6% each) — significance of non-regional dominance
India's shareholding rank and voting weight vs China's relatively lower share
Membership eligibility: open to UN members and its specialized agencies in the Asia-Pacific region

concepts.name: ADB's Organizational Governance Structure
key_dimensions: Board of Governors (supreme body) → Board of Directors (12 directors) → President
Convention that the ADB President is always Japanese — compare with World Bank (American) and IMF (European)
Resident missions vs headquarters functions — decentralization policy
Distinction between ADB's governance and AIIB's governance as a UPSC comparison trap

concepts.name: ADB's Capital Structure and Funding Windows
key_dimensions: Ordinary Capital Resources (OCR) — loans to middle-income countries at near-market rates
Asian Development Fund (ADF) — concessional window for poorest members, now merged into OCR (2017)
Technical Assistance Special Fund (TASF) — grants for capacity building
ADB's AAA credit rating and its significance for borrowing on international capital markets

concepts.name: ADB's Merger of ADF with OCR (2017 Reform)
key_dimensions: Rationale: Expand concessional lending capacity without additional capital contributions
Impact on India: India became eligible for concessional-rate OCR loans post-merger
Distinction between pre-2017 and post-2017 lending modalities — a frequent exam confusion area
Comparison with IDA-IBRD separation at World Bank — why ADB chose merger vs World Bank's separation

concepts.name: ADB's Strategic Priorities: Strategy 2030
key_dimensions: Seven operational priorities: prosperous, inclusive, resilient, sustainable Asia-Pacific
Focus areas: gender equality, climate change, private sector development, regional cooperation
Shift from infrastructure-only to broader sustainable development — contrast with earlier Strategy 2020
Climate finance commitment: 75% of projects to have climate components by 2030

concepts.name: ADB and Climate Finance
key_dimensions: Commitment to provide $100 billion in climate financing from 2019–2030
Energy Transition Mechanism (ETM) — early retirement of coal plants in Southeast Asia
Green bonds and blue bonds issued by ADB — distinction and purpose
ADB's role in Paris Agreement implementation vs Green Climate Fund (GCF) — overlap and distinction

concepts.name: ADB vs AIIB: Key Comparative Dimensions
key_dimensions: AIIB: China-led (2016), infrastructure focus; ADB: Japan/US-led (1966), broader mandate — UPSC favorite trap
Membership overlap: India is a member of both — strategic implications
Headquarters: AIIB in Beijing vs ADB in Manila
Complementarity vs competition narrative — co-financing agreements between ADB and AIIB

concepts.name: ADB vs World Bank Group: Structural Differences
key_dimensions: ADB's regional focus vs World Bank's global mandate
ADB has no equivalent of IFC (private sector arm) separately — private sector operations within ADB itself
ADB's President selection (regional convention) vs World Bank President (US convention)
Concessional windows: ADF (now merged) vs IDA — differences in eligibility criteria

concepts.name: India's Engagement with ADB
key_dimensions: India is among the top borrowers from ADB — sectors: urban infrastructure, transport, energy, health
India not eligible for ADF historically (middle-income country) — changed post-2017 OCR-ADF merger
ADB's Country Partnership Strategy with India — current focus areas
State-level lending: ADB directly lends to Indian states (e.g., for urban projects) — federal dimension

concepts.name: ADB's Private Sector Operations
key_dimensions: ADB can lend directly to private entities without sovereign guarantee — unlike some MDB windows
Non-Sovereign Operations (NSO) — equity investments, guarantees, and loans to private sector
Office of Public-Private Partnership (OPPP) — facilitating PPP frameworks in member countries
Comparison with IFC (World Bank's private sector arm) — IFC is a separate entity, ADB's private ops are internal

concepts.name: ADB's Role in Regional Cooperation and Integration
key_dimensions: Greater Mekong Subregion (GMS) Program — flagship regional cooperation initiative
Central Asia Regional Economic Cooperation (CAREC) — connectivity with Central Asia
South Asia Subregional Economic Cooperation (SASEC) — India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Nepal connectivity
ASEAN Infrastructure Fund (AIF) — ADB's role as administrator

concepts.name: ADB's Safeguard Policies
key_dimensions: Safeguard Policy Statement (SPS) 2009 — three pillars: environment, involuntary resettlement, indigenous peoples
Distinction from World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) — UPSC comparison trap
Accountability Mechanism: Compliance Review Panel (CRP) and Problem-Solving function
Civil society and NGO engagement requirements under ADB's public communications policy

concepts.name: ADB's Concessional Lending Criteria and Graduation Policy
key_dimensions: Countries graduate from concessional loans based on GNI per capita thresholds
Blend countries (eligible for both concessional and market-rate loans) — India's historical blend status
Graduation implications: how countries like China transitioned from borrowers to donors/shareholders
Comparison with World Bank's IDA graduation policy — similar but distinct thresholds

concepts.name: ADB's Response to COVID-19 and Health Financing
key_dimensions: $20 billion COVID-19 response package — rapid financing facility deployment
Asia Pacific Vaccine Access Facility (APVAX) — ADB's role distinct from COVAX (WHO-led)
Health sector lending expansion — shift from traditional infrastructure bias
Lessons for pandemic preparedness financing architecture in Asia

concepts.name: ADB and Gender Mainstreaming
key_dimensions: Gender equity as a 'driver of change' under Strategy 2030
Gender Action Plan — mandatory gender categorization of all ADB projects
Women's Livelihood Bond and other gender-focused financial instruments
Comparison with World Bank's Women Entrepreneurs Finance Initiative (We-Fi) — overlap area

concepts.name: ADB's Technical Assistance (TA) Operations
key_dimensions: Four types: project preparatory TA, capacity development TA, research TA, regional TA
TA funded through TASF, Japan Fund, and other bilateral trust funds — multilateral-bilateral nexus
Knowledge products: Asian Development Outlook (ADO) — ADB's flagship economic publication
Distinction between TA grants and regular loans — no repayment obligation for TA grants

concepts.name: ADB's Asian Development Outlook (ADO)
key_dimensions: Flagship annual economic publication — equivalent to World Bank's World Development Report or IMF's WEO
Covers GDP growth forecasts, inflation, trade for developing Asia — frequently cited in UPSC current affairs
UPSC trap: ADO is ADB's report; confusing it with ADB's Annual Report or AIIB's reports
Special thematic focus each year — past themes include food security, digital economy, climate

concepts.name: ADB's Relationship with ASEAN and Pacific Island Nations
key_dimensions: Pacific Approach — special concessional terms for small Pacific island developing states (PIDS)
Pacific Private Sector Development Initiative (PSDI) — dedicated Pacific program
ADB as primary MDB for Pacific island nations — World Bank and ADB complementarity/overlap
ASEAN Infrastructure Fund (AIF): ADB as administrator but ASEAN members as equity holders

concepts.name: ADB's Anticorruption and Integrity Framework
key_dimensions: Office of Anticorruption and Integrity (OAI) — investigates fraud and corruption in ADB-financed projects
Debarment policy — sanctions firms/individuals; cross-debarment agreement with World Bank Group
Integrity Due Diligence (IDD) — applied to private sector clients
Distinction: OAI investigates project-level corruption; does not rate member country governance (unlike World Bank's CPIA)
